articles.title: A Review on Mechanisms of Action and Signaling Pathways of Natural Anti-hyperpigmentation Agents.
articles.abstract: Hyperpigmentation is a dermatological condition characterized by excessive melanin production, resulting in skin darkening. Intrinsic and extrinsic mediators, including ultraviolet (UV) radiation, hormonal changes, inflammation, and genetic predisposition, contribute to hyperpigmentation pathogenesis. The current review thoroughly examines the biological processes involved in hyperpigmentation, with particular emphasis on its signaling pathways, particularly the cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP), wingless-related integration site (Wnt)/β-catenin, phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K)/protein kinase B (Akt), and mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK), thereby providing mechanistic insights that may facilitate the development of effective treatments. The review also evaluates the safety, toxicity, and therapeutic efficacy of TYR inhibitors, arbutin, azelaic acid, ellagic acid, kojic acid, resveratrol, and the melanosome inhibitor niacinamide, for managing hyperpigmentation. Additionally, the review summarizes the in vitro and in vivo studies of these agents and other emerging plant extracts. Recent advances in the use of plant extracts for hyperpigmentation have shown promising efficacy; nevertheless, their translation into clinical and commercial applications remains limited. This limited translation might be attributed to the challenges related to standardization and the paucity of clinical evidence regarding long-term safety. Moreover, ongoing studies on natural anti-hyperpigmentation agents have highlighted the critical role of patent analyses in the advancement of biomedical research. This review provides a strategic direction for researchers to assess the safety, efficacy, and toxicity profiles of natural anti-hyperpigmentation agents.

articles.title: Current and Emerging Drug Therapy for Acne Vulgaris: A Comprehensive Review.
articles.abstract: Acne vulgaris is a highly prevalent chronic inflammatory disorder of the pilosebaceous unit that affects the majority of adolescents and young adults. Its pathogenesis is multifactorial and is driven largely by hormonal dysregulation, which promotes excess sebum production and follicular hyperkeratinisation, resulting in pore occlusion and the characteristic inflammatory lesions accompanied by swelling and erythema. Acne is caused by Cutibacterium acnes, which colonizes and activates acquired and innate immune responses. Acne is also produced owing to stimulation of the IGF-1 factor, disturbance of the omega-3 and omega-6 cycles, suppression of FoxO1, and activation of mTORC1, which assists in boosting sebum production. Proven treatments target these mechanisms by utilizing systemic and topical drug-delivery systems. Topical retinoids, which have antiinflammatory and anti-acne properties, such as azelaic acid, benzoyl peroxide, salicylic acid, dapsone, and topical or oral antibiotics, are used to treat acne. However, these formulations have limitations, including the need for prolonged treatment, persistent skin irritation, and the development of antibiotic resistance. To overcome these limitations, novel approaches have been utilized, including AI, nano-based formulations, nanoemulsions, semi-synthetic formulations, and herbal formulations. Recent improvements in acne therapy have focused on enhancing effectiveness and safety. The goal of recent developments in acne therapy is to improve treatment efficacy and safety. New drug delivery systems incorporating nanotechnology improve targeting of damaged areas and reduce side effects.

articles.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) lacks disease‑modifying therapies. The infrapatellar fat pad (IPFP) is hypothesized to regulate joint metabolism, but its molecular effectors are unknown. We investigated whether IPFP‑derived metabolites protect cartilage via lipid‑metabolizing enzymes.

articles.title: Topical treatment of rosacea: update and outlook.
articles.abstract: Rosacea is an inflammatory skin condition that typically requires long term management. It is characterized by redness of the face, dilation of facial capillaries, the appearance of pimples and pustules, and it may lead to advanced conditions such as skin lymphoedema and rhinophyma. Initially, treatment involved oral drug administration, but a number of topical formulations have been developed as medicines to manage this skin disorder. Many rosacea patients have sensitive skin and side effects from current topical therapies have been shown to impact seriously on patient adherence to topical therapy regimens and clinical success. Notwithstanding this, no new topical products for management of rosacea have been made available since 2015. This review considers alternative formulation strategies that have been investigated for the most commonly prescribed topical drugs for rosacea, namely, metronidazole, azelaic acid and ivermectin. The pharmacokinetics and metabolism of each molecule are also discussed as this information is an essential starting point for required local tissue target concentrations. Attention is focused on evaluation of formulations with either in vitro permeation testing or in vivo studies. Finally, the limitations of studies published to date are highlighted as well as the likely barriers hindering translation of novel therapies from the laboratory to the market.

articles.title: Polymeric Azelaic Acid-loaded Nanocapsules Incorporated into Tragacanth Gum: Development and Biological Evaluation in Alternative Models for the Treatment of Rosacea.
articles.abstract: Rosacea is an inflammatory skin disorder that significantly impairs patients' quality of life. Azelaic acid (AZA), a well-established keratolytic and anti-inflammatory agent; however, its clinical application is often limited by local adverse effects that reduce patient adherence. In this context, nanotechnology-based drug delivery systems, particularly polymeric nanocapsules, represent a promising strategy to improve physicochemical stability, reduce cutaneous irritation, and enable incorporation into semi-solid formulations with enhanced skin interaction. This study aimed to develop and characterize AZA-loaded polymeric nanocapsules incorporated into tragacanth gum-based hydrogels as a safe, effective, and patient-friendly therapeutic alternative for rosacea. The nanocapsules exhibited a uniform nanometric size (185.66 ± 2.08 nm), low polydispersity index (0.12 ± 0.02), slightly negative zeta potential (- 8.67 ± 0.26 mV), and a skin-compatible acidic pH (3.56 ± 0.16). Drug loading reached 0.53 mg/mL, with an encapsulation efficiency of 42.20%. In vitro cytocompatibility assays showed cell viability close to 100% after 12 and 24 h of exposure, confirming the safety of the system. Antiangiogenic assays using chicken embryos further supported its biocompatibility. The hydrogels displayed a slightly acidic pH and pseudoplastic flow behavior described by the Herschel-Bulkley model, along with higher adhesiveness than liquid suspensions, favoring topical application. Both conventional AZA hydrogels (TG-AZA) and nanocapsule-based hydrogels (TG-NC-AZA) promoted effective drug retention within the stratum corneum. Notably, TG-NC-AZA showed a non-irritant profile in HET-CAM and CAM-TBS assays and demonstrated pronounced anti-inflammatory activity, achieving a 75% reduction. Overall, these findings highlight TG-NC-AZA as an innovative and clinically relevant therapeutic approach for rosacea.

articles.title: Azelaic acid delays aging and prolongs lifespan via resisting oxidation stress mediated by IIS pathway coupling hsf-1 in C. elegans.
articles.abstract: Azelaic acid (AzA), an antioxidant and anti-inflammatory compound from cereals used in food preservatives and cosmetics, was investigated for anti-aging effects in Caenorhabditis elegans. AzA improved locomotive activities and muscle morphology during aging, extended lifespan under both normal and oxidative stress conditions, and reduced paralysis in neurodegenerative models. It decreased reactive oxygen species levels and enhanced superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity and SOD-3 protein expression. Quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) analysis revealed that AzA differentially regulated oxidative stress-related genes including daf-2, daf-16, skn-1, and hsf-1 under normal and oxidative stress conditions. Mechanistically, the lifespan extension conferred by AzA under oxidative stress was abolished in daf-16(mu86), daf-2(e1370), and hsf-1(sy441) mutants, indicating that these genes are essential for AzA-mediated anti-aging effects. These findings suggest that azelaic acid is a potential anti-aging candidate.

articles.title: Treatment of Refractory Centrofacial Melasma in a 64-Year-Old Female Using the NewMelan Depigmentation System: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Melasma is a chronic acquired hyperpigmentation disorder that commonly affects sun-exposed areas of the face and may significantly impact quality of life. Treatment can be challenging because of frequent recurrence and variable responses to conventional therapies. This case report describes the management of refractory facial melasma in a 64-year-old patient with a history of prolonged ultraviolet exposure and persistent facial hyperpigmentation. The patient previously underwent multiple treatment modalities, including chemical peels, mechanical peels, and laser-based therapies, without achieving satisfactory clinical improvement. Due to the limited response to these conventional approaches, treatment with the NewMelan Depigmentation System, a topical depigmenting formulation containing arbutin 1.5%, kojic acid 1%, and azelaic acid 1.5%, was initiated. The treatment protocol consisted of topical application three times daily during the first week, twice daily during the second week, and once daily during the subsequent two weeks, followed by maintenance therapy and continued photoprotection. Progressive reduction in facial hyperpigmentation was observed throughout the treatment period. After one month of therapy, the pigmentation became markedly less noticeable, resulting in substantial cosmetic improvement and high patient satisfaction. Continued maintenance treatment and daily sun protection contributed to preservation of the clinical outcome. This case highlights the potential role of the NewMelan Depigmentation System as a therapeutic option for patients with refractory facial melasma who have not responded adequately to conventional treatment modalities. Further clinical studies are warranted to evaluate long-term outcomes, safety, and efficacy in larger patient populations.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of a novel anhydrous 0.1% retinal and 10% azelaic acid concentrate for blemish-prone skin: An eight-week randomized prospective split-face, vehicle-controlled study.
articles.abstract: Blemish-prone skin is driven by follicular hyperkeratinization, excessive sebum production, microbial dysbiosis and inflammation, often accompanied by post-inflammatory erythema and hyperpigmentation. Retinal and azelaic acid are established topical actives with complementary mechanisms of action, yet no clinical study has evaluated their combination in a single formulation.

articles.title: Expression of interleukins in adult female acne: evaluating the effects of azelaic acid.
articles.abstract: Adult female acne (AFA) is a multifactorial skin condition that affects women aged > 25 years, with inflammation playing a central role in its aetiopathogenesis. However, most research has primarily focused on severe acne vulgaris, while the immunological mechanisms underlying AFA remain poorly understood.
